transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Yeah, well, I guess what made me come in is that the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling really flat and heavy. I just stopped initiating them. Like my photography walks, or mentoring the kids, or even just keeping a clean calendar. 

I'm an executive secretary, so calendars are basically my whole world. My boss, Mr. Henderson, he actually refuses to use Outlook for his personal appointments, which means I have to write them all in this massive leather planner he bought on a trip to Italy. It's a nice planner, I guess, the leather smells really rich, but he insists on using these blue gel pens that just smear everywhere if you aren't perfectly careful. I usually love organizing it, though. I usually take a lot of pride in getting it just right. 

Just like my photography, really. I have this vintage Nikon I usually take down to the river on the weekends. I caught a really great shot of a blue heron down there last spring, just standing perfectly still in the reeds. The lighting was incredible that day. But lately... I don't know. I just don't have the drive to pick up the camera or even color-code the schedule. Everything just feels heavy, and I just can't bring myself to start doing any of it anymore.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Down? No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or tearful or anything like that most of the day. I'm not sitting around crying. Actually, I tried to watch a sad movie the other night, thinking maybe I just needed a good cry to sort of shake this off, you know? I put on that one with Tom Hanks, where he's stuck on the island. My sister absolutely loves that movie. She actually went to Fiji for her honeymoon, which is near where they filmed it, I think. She brought back this really beautiful carved wooden turtle for me. It sits on my desk at work right next to Mr. Henderson's inbox. He's always knocking it over when he drops off his dry cleaning receipts... he goes to this place on 4th Street that uses the most awful smelling starch, I swear. But um... what was the question? Oh, feeling depressed. No, I haven't really noticed feeling sad. Just that flat feeling I mentioned.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like your photography walks or mentoring the kids?

Yeah, exactly. I mean, I think I said that right at the start, didn't I? The photography, the mentoring... it all just feels so heavy. I just don't initiate any of it anymore. The kids at the mentoring program, they're usually so full of energy. There's this one kid, Leo, who is absolutely obsessed with trains. He knows every single subway route in the city by heart. It's actually incredible. His mom works night shifts at the hospital downtown, the one with the really aggressive seagulls in the parking lot. I parked there once when I was visiting my cousin after she had her appendix out, and one of those gulls literally swooped down and stole a French fry right out of my hand. I had gotten them from this little diner across the street, which honestly had the best fries I've ever had, perfectly crispy. But anyway, yeah, I just... I haven't been going to see the kids. Or taking pictures. The interest just isn't there. It's all just flat.
Have you been feeling fatigued or lacking energy lately, even when you haven't been doing much physically?

Fatigued? Um, no, not really. I wouldn't say my body feels tired or anything. I have normal energy, I guess. I still make my morning coffee every day at exactly 6:15. Actually, Mr. Henderson just bought this massive, incredibly complicated espresso machine for the office. It's Italian, just like his leather planner. He insisted we needed it for "office morale," but it has all these pressure dials and steam wands that absolutely no one knows how to use. He tried to descale it himself last Tuesday and ended up spraying boiling water all over the main copier. It was a complete disaster. 

The repair guy who had to come out and fix the copier was this huge guy, must have been six-foot-six at least, and he kept bumping his head on the hanging plants in the lobby. We have these really beautiful pothos plants that Susan from accounting brought in after her mother passed away. They grow so fast if you just give them a little bit of indirect sunlight. Susan has a real green thumb, unlike me... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being tired. No, physically my energy is fine. I'm not tired. It's just that flat feeling I was talking about.
Have you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, over the last two weeks?

Hopeless? No, I wouldn't use that word. I don't feel hopeless or sad, really. Just... you know, that flat thing. Like I'm just going through the motions. Speaking of going through the motions, I had to organize all the files for the quarterly review yesterday. Mr. Henderson is so particular about how they're labeled. He uses this specific brand of label maker that you can only buy at this one office supply store three towns over. I had to drive all the way out there last month just to get replacement tape. The drive wasn't too bad, though. I took the scenic route past the old reservoir. It's really beautiful out there this time of year, all the leaves are turning. There's this little farm stand on the corner where they sell the most amazing apple cider donuts. They're still warm when you buy them, and they just coat your fingers in cinnamon sugar. I bought a dozen and brought them into the office, but Susan wouldn't eat any because she's on this new keto diet. She's been eating nothing but hard-boiled eggs and avocado for three weeks. The smell in the breakroom is honestly criminal. But yeah, no, I don't feel down or hopeless. Just... flat.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks or more?

Down or depressed? No, I... I think I just answered that, right? With the hopeless question? I don't feel sad or depressed. Just flat. It's funny you ask the same thing twice, though, it reminds me of this time at work when Mr. Henderson asked me to double-check the minutes from the board meeting. He was convinced I had missed a motion about the new parking lot paving contract. The paving company they hired, by the way, they left this massive pile of gravel taking up three visitor spots for an entire week. The delivery guy from the deli—the one who brings us those incredible pastrami sandwiches on rye, the bread is always perfectly toasted—he had to park halfway down the street and walk all the lunches in the pouring rain. His umbrella flipped inside out because the wind gets so crazy coming off the building. He was completely soaked. But anyway, yeah, I checked the minutes, and the motion wasn't there because they hadn't actually voted on it. So, no, I'm not depressed. Just flat, like I said.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even when you have the opportunity to do them?

Well, yeah, that's actually why I'm here. It's the flat feeling I've been trying to explain. The things that usually make me feel like myself—like my photography walks, or mentoring the kids at the community center, or even just keeping my calendar perfectly clean and color-coded—they just started feeling so heavy and... flat. I just stopped initiating them. I don't even pick up my camera anymore. 

Which is a shame, really, because I have this beautiful vintage Leica that I found at an estate sale three years ago. The guy who owned it was a retired architect, and his house was incredible. Mid-century modern, lots of glass and exposed beams, nestled right up against this wooded hill. He had an entire room dedicated just to his model trains. And I mean an entire room—the tracks went through the walls and over these little custom-built bridges. His daughter was running the sale, and she told me he used to spend hours just watching the trains go around. She was selling all these amazing vintage clothes, too. I bought a tweed jacket that fits me perfectly, though I haven't worn it lately because of this whole... heavy feeling. It's just sitting in the closet next to my camera bag. But yeah, I just don't have the drive to do any of my usual things right now.
Can you recall if you've felt a depressed mood, like feeling sad or empty, most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row recently?

I... I feel like we're going in circles here. Empty, sad, down, depressed... I keep saying no, but it's like you're waiting for me to say yes. I don't feel sad. I feel flat. Just flat. 

It reminds me of when my sister tried to convince me to buy this specific car. She was so sure I needed a Honda Civic. She kept sending me links to all these different Civics—blue ones, silver ones, ones with sunroofs. She even dragged me to the dealership on a Saturday morning. The salesman there, his name was Gary, he had this really loud tie with little golf clubs all over it. He kept trying to offer us complimentary coffee, but the machine was broken, so it just kept making this awful grinding noise. Anyway, I kept telling her I didn't want a Civic, I wanted something with more cargo space for my photography gear, back when I was actually taking photos. But she just kept showing me Civics, like if she showed me enough of them, I'd suddenly want one. 

So, no. Not sad. Not empty. Just flat.
Has there been a time in the past two weeks when you felt absolutely no interest or pleasure in doing something you used to genuinely enjoy, even if just for a few moments?

Again with the interest thing? I mean... I feel like we just talked about this, right? The photography, the calendar... it's all just been flat. I haven't really enjoyed any of it. 

It's kind of like... well, speaking of calendars, my old boss, Mr. Henderson, he used to use this huge desk calendar. Like, one of those massive paper ones that takes up the whole blotter? He insisted on writing everything in pencil, but he pressed so hard that even when he erased something, you could still read the indentation. It drove me crazy when I had to update his schedule. I actually bought him a really nice set of erasable pens for Boss's Day once. The ink was blue, but it erased completely clean. The packaging said it used some sort of friction-activated thermal ink. Fascinating technology, really. They sell them at that little stationery shop downtown, the one next to the bakery that makes those amazing lemon tarts. The baker there, she always wears these bright floral aprons. I think she makes them herself. 

But anyway, yeah, no interest. Just like I was saying before. Everything's just... flat.
